voices.speaker: Tan-chun and Bao-chai
voices.guidance: Tan-chun enjoys play but respects delegated authority. Bao-chai's risk awareness, learning and affection do not make her an all-knowing expositor. Her views about women's reputation remain hers, alongside her own excellent literary criticism.

voices.speaker: Bao-yu and Dai-yu
voices.guidance: Keep quick wit, intimacy, embarrassment and unequal knowledge. Bao-yu's kindness does not certify his economic or political judgments. Dai-yu's accidental hurt to Cai-yun is acknowledged, not turned into deliberate cruelty.

voices.speaker: Xiang-yun and Caltrop
voices.guidance: Xiang-yun is exuberant and competitive, with expert knowledge and conspicuous mistakes. Caltrop's learning is eager and real; her naivety does not make her stupid. Her skirt anxiety concerns relationships and household rebuke as well as cost.

voices.speaker: Parfumée and the actresses
voices.guidance: Parfumée is proud, energetic, theatrical and capable of puncturing Bao-yu's pomp. Male costume and names do not change the girls' sex or narrator pronouns. Distinguish her enacted song voice from her everyday speech.

voices.speaker: Xiu-yan and Adamantina
voices.guidance: Xiu-yan can call her old friend eccentric while gratefully acknowledging her teaching. Adamantina's voice reaches the reader through a formal card and reported views, not an invented encounter.

voices.speaker: You-shi
voices.guidance: Her funeral decisions are capable and immediate. Her later unsuccessful resistance to the secret marriage is explicit. Neither kinship ambiguity nor a repeated family name should transport her into scenes where she is absent.

voices.speaker: Jia Zhen, Jia Rong and Jia Lian
voices.guidance: Give each man his own mixture of desire, opportunism, bluster and evasive respectability. Retain coercion and misuse of hierarchy. Their compliments and Jia Rong's reports are not reliable narratorial endorsements.

voices.speaker: You Er-jie and You San-jie
voices.guidance: The elder sister's softness, hope and admitted past differ from the younger's combative manipulation, tears and demand for choice. Keep their contradictions and the narrator's judgments without sanitizing or romanticizing them.

voices.speaker: Bao Er's wife, the pages and Joker
voices.guidance: Use forceful obscenity at its actual intensity, including anatomical insults and the mother-directed threat. The pages' innuendo is not a licensed expansion into explicit acts. Joker performs for his new audience; retain his prejudice and flattery as speech.

scenes.title: The side-gate exchange
scenes.guidance: Continue the interrupted laugh in 60.45, now with Mrs Liu's sexually coarse insults. Fruit is guarded under the garden arrangements, not freely available. The boy's sister address for Wu-er does not establish kinship.

scenes.title: Eggs and kitchen allowances
scenes.guidance: Lotus brings Chess's demand. Ten or so reserved eggs contradict an absolute empty-kitchen reading, but not Mrs Liu's complaint about scarcity. Her account of budgets, favours and prices is interested speech. Keep the food distinctions and the escalating class insults.

scenes.title: Chess attacks the kitchen
scenes.guidance: Lotus embellishes her account. Chess orders destruction, but the maids do not finish throwing everything away. Chess tips out the delivered egg dish; the messenger conceals that fact from the kitchen.

scenes.title: A gift becomes evidence
scenes.guidance: Wu-er divides the fuling frost, gives a packet to Swallow for Parfumée and lies about why she entered the garden. Suspicion, discovery of rose essence and seizure of the remaining frost follow. A lie about entry does not prove either theft.

scenes.title: Punishment suspended
scenes.guidance: Scribe relays Tan-chun's referral. Xi-feng orders forty blows for each woman, dismissal and disposal of Wu-er; Patience delays these punishments. Detention overnight, humiliation and lack of water or bedding are actually experienced.

scenes.title: Patience traces the gifts
scenes.guidance: Aroma knows only the first transfer; Parfumée confirms the next. Bao-yu worries about the gatekeeper uncle and offers cover stories. Skybright names Cai-yun, Patience explains her prior suspicions, and the three raised fingers reveal concern for Tan-chun only to the people present.

scenes.title: Confession and cover story
scenes.guidance: Patience's claim that the frightened suspect has confessed is a tactic, not a new fact. Cai-yun admits taking things at Aunt Zhao's request and giving them to Jia Huan. They agree that Bao-yu will bear the blame; Wu-er is taught another account of the frost's source.

scenes.title: Restoring kitchen authority
scenes.guidance: Qin Xian's wife has only a temporary appointment. Patience tells Lin Zhi-xiao's wife and Xi-feng the agreed cover story. The unopened baskets are real corroboration against this theft, not proof that every part of the cover story is true. Xi-feng's further torture proposal remains unexecuted. Patience invokes their eventual allegiance to Jia She's branch.

scenes.title: The case ends, jealousy does not
scenes.guidance: Mrs Liu and Wu-er return to their former position, which does not itself give Wu-er a new post in Bao-yu's rooms. Qin Xian's wife loses the kitchen and the value of her gifts. Jia Huan throws back Cai-yun's gifts; Cai-yun, not Aunt Zhao, throws them into the river.

scenes.title: Four shared birthdays
scenes.guidance: The four are Bao-yu, Bao-qin, Xing Xiu-yan and Patience. Preserve ceremonial visits, reciprocal bows and hierarchy. Tan-chun first forgets February birthdays and is corrected. Her two-table order is an extra private feast, not the final total of tables.

scenes.title: Gathering at Red Fragrance Court
scenes.guidance: Bao-chai locks the connecting gate and warns privately of other serious problems without naming them. Patience receives and redistributes birthday gifts before arriving. Aunt Xue withdraws to the council hall. Preserve all four tables and the two women storytellers' reassignment.

scenes.title: Two kinds of drinking game
scenes.guidance: The concealed-word game and finger-guessing run alongside each other. Keep the clue relationships, speakers, penalties, five-source composite lines and puns. Caltrop knows poetry; she is inexperienced in this game, not illiterate. Dai-yu's theft joke targets Bao-yu but inadvertently hurts Cai-yun.

scenes.title: Xiang-yun asleep among peonies
scenes.guidance: The housekeepers inspect decorum. Xiang-yun is discovered on a damp stone seat with petals, fan, scarf-pillow, bees and butterflies. Her dream speech continues the drinking rules. Tea, a sobering stone and sour soup are historical responses, not medical advice.

scenes.title: Authority, economy and shared tea
scenes.guidance: Tan-chun's two eyes belong to a go position; the repeated human eyes make a small verbal echo. Cai-er's mother is dismissed provisionally pending Lady Wang's return. Dai-yu recognises overspending; Bao-yu assumes their own supply cannot fail. Two cups are brought: Bao-chai sips Dai-yu's cup, which Dai-yu finishes.

scenes.title: Parfumée's meal and Wu-er's place
scenes.guidance: Parfumée resents being left out, asks for a simple meal and receives richer food. Preserve who eats which portion without inventing a fourth pastry's destination. Bao-yu says Wu-er may enter tomorrow; actual arrival remains delayed in 63.2. Aroma's teasing recalls Skybright's work on the peacock-gold coat.

scenes.title: Plant play and the red skirt
scenes.guidance: The plant-name contest becomes rough play, leaving Caltrop's new skirt wet and dirty. Keep Dou-guan's sexual taunt and Caltrop's indignation. Aroma willingly brings her matching skirt. Bao-yu turns away for the change, then buries the paired plants among fallen flowers, not the skirt. Zhen-er says Second Miss without an unsupported named identification.

scenes.title: Preparing the private birthday feast
scenes.guidance: Keep eight contributors and the full 3.2-tael total. Prefer leave or absence for 有假的, with the lexical reservation recorded separately. Wu-er is still ill. The inspection precedes the closed doors. Musk's sentence retains its negative about good intentions and her subsequent explanation of caution.

scenes.title: Informality and invitations
scenes.guidance: Dress and hair changes loosen formal ceremony without stripping anyone naked. All actresses remain girls. Forty small dishes, circular kang tables and chair placement matter. Invitations widen from maids to the girls; Bao-qin and Li Wan are explicitly fetched. Do not invent an arrival explanation for Xiang-yun.

scenes.title: Eight flower lots
scenes.guidance: Keep all eight drawings, inscriptions, poems, rules and reactions. There is no lot for Bao-yu. Parfumée's birthday opening is interrupted; the replacement song is complete. Bao-yu's repeated peony line and gaze at Parfumée remain. The lots are play and suggestive imagery, not a narrator's forecast of later events.

scenes.title: Late dispersal and morning after
scenes.guidance: Keep the eleven clock strokes beside the traditional time expression without forced minute conversion. The servants continue until the fourth watch. Aroma moves the drunk Parfumée beside Bao-yu and sleeps opposite. Neither sexual contact nor intent is supplied. Patience was not at this night feast, despite providing its wine.

scenes.title: Adamantina's card
scenes.guidance: Si-er received and forgot the card; Adamantina did not visit. Xiu-yan explains their ten-year neighbour and partial-teacher relationship. Preserve threshold and worldly-outsider wordplay, both complete private cards and the two-line grave image. Bao-yu slips his reply through the closed gate.

scenes.title: Costume, empire and renaming
scenes.guidance: Track Parfumée's successive male and foreign-sounding aliases; keep Kui-guan and Dou-guan separate. Bao-yu's imperial boasting and ethnic disparagement are his words, answered by Parfumée's challenge. The narrator separately states the households possess captured slaves. The Glass nickname must never merge Parfumée with Grandmother Jia's maid Glass.

scenes.title: Celebration cut short
scenes.guidance: Patience's return feast is at Elm-shade Hall; roughly twenty play pass-the-flower. The Zhen visitors occasion the women managers' exit, but their business is not supplied. Swing jokes precede the abrupt death announcement. The servant's imperial death euphemism is a misuse, not news of the emperor's death.

scenes.title: You-shi handles Jia Jing's funeral
scenes.guidance: You-shi detains the Daoists, consults physicians, moves and coffins the body because of the heat. Distinguish the physicians' account from the Daoists' evasions. The officials obtain leave and a posthumous fifth-rank appointment. Keep the Board's memorial separate from the emperor's edict across the block boundary. Jia Bin and Jia Guang escort Grandmother Jia.

scenes.title: Jia Rong at the house
scenes.guidance: You-shi's stepmother and her two daughters are present while You-shi is at the temple. Jia Rong's erotic teasing, touching and boasts violate kinship and mourning decorum. The sisters' resistance, laughter and insults all remain. His claims about others stay his claims.

scenes.title: The coffin enters the city
scenes.guidance: The fourth day of an unspecified lunar month and mao hour mark departure; arrival is between wei and shen. The spectacle and the half-learned criticism coexist. Mourning restrictions do not stop the men's clandestine conduct. Do not align this date with the later wedding on a third lunar month-day by inventing a month.

scenes.title: Leisure and a mourning fan-case
scenes.guidance: The girls play jacks for melon seeds; Skybright chases Parfumée. Aroma's meditation is her excuse while making a new mourning cord and fan-case. The old one dates to Qin-shi's funeral. Bao-yu's tea is cooled in fresh well-water, not by ice.

scenes.title: Dai-yu's private offering and poems
scenes.guidance: Snowgoose does not know the rite's purpose. Bao-yu guesses; the later smoke and leftover libation show only that a rite occurred. Preserve his unfinished declaration, their mutual tears and Nightingale's mistaken assumption of a quarrel. The poems' privacy becomes a discussion of female reputation; no reader note should disclose a definite dedicatee.

scenes.title: Five poems, five reversals
scenes.guidance: Translate all five headings and twenty lines, and Bao-chai's four quoted lines. Keep each poem's argument and unsettling historical judgment. Bao-yu supplies the collection title afterwards. Bao-chai's accomplished criticism sits beside her restriction on public female talent.

scenes.title: The travellers return
scenes.guidance: Jia Lian precedes the elders. Grandmother Jia's illness and treatment delay her participation; the coffin returns to the temple and removal to the family's native place after the hundred days is still future. You-shi and the men remain at the temple; her stepmother and sisters mind the house.

scenes.title: Desire, debt and a scheme
scenes.guidance: At 64.43, the You sisters are You Er-jie and You San-jie, not You-shi. The narrator states sexual and family impropriety, while Jia Rong promotes a secret second household for his own access. Preserve 1,110, 500, 610, 500, 200 and 300 taels in their separate accounts. Jia Lian undertakes the shortage to gain an excuse to visit. His praise of You Er-jie is interested speech.

scenes.title: The betel purse and jade pendant
scenes.guidance: Track the purse, half-chewed betel, silk handkerchief and Jia Lian's nine-dragon jade pendant separately from the funeral money. You Er-jie secretly takes the returned object. Jia Rong manages departures and reports his own proposal as Jia Lian's request.

scenes.title: Consent, coercion and preparations
scenes.guidance: You-shi objects and is overruled; she does not arrange the match willingly. You Er-jie assents, but the Zhang family is coerced into cancelling the prior betrothal. The payment is twenty taels, not the earlier estimate. The present source supplies Bao Er and his wife without the public edition's added remarriage backstory.

scenes.title: The secret second marriage
scenes.guidance: Mother and younger sister move in on the second day of an unspecified lunar month; You Er-jie arrives before dawn on its third day. Plain dress reflects mourning and secrecy. The marriage and sexual relationship are explicit, but the source declines detail. Jia Lian orders everyone to call her mistress and mentally displaces Xi-feng.

scenes.title: Jia Zhen visits the new household
scenes.guidance: About two months pass. The mother and elder sister withdraw, leaving Jia Zhen and You San-jie. The source leaves what follows unspecified. Bao Er's wife's obscene abuse and practical control are not softened. The three pages give transparent excuses; their horses' clash and the bed-sharing obscenity remain without invented sexual choreography.

scenes.title: You San-jie confronts the men
scenes.guidance: You Er-jie acknowledges her past and worries for her sister. Jia Lian attempts complicity with Jia Zhen. You San-jie names their treatment of the sisters as prostitutes, threatens them and controls the gathering. Preserve both her agency and the text's erotic and moral judgments; do not retrofit another edition's innocence narrative.

scenes.title: Marriage proposed, identity withheld
scenes.guidance: The narrator's moral verdict, Jia Lian's forgiving speech and the couple's attachment are different layers. Retain 如胶授漆 without Chinese emendation. You San-jie requires a man of her own choice. Jia Lian wrongly guesses Bao-yu. The title names Liu, but the dialogue reveals only a five-years-ago hint here.

scenes.title: Joker describes the Rong household
scenes.guidance: This is a drinking servant's flattering, hostile and partial account. Preserve Xi-feng's alleged cruelty, Patience's constrained position, the girls' nicknames and the wind-and-snow compliment without converting them to neutral character summaries. 尤氏 at 65.31 is You Er-jie; 尤氏姊妹 at 65.36 are the two sisters.

quantitiesAndChronology.guidance: Mrs Liu reports ten cash per egg, four or five buyers gathering two thousand eggs, and ten or so eggs reserved for garnishes. The garden kitchen serves forty or fifty people with two chickens, two ducks, ten-odd catties of meat and a string of cash for vegetables per day, for two meals. Keep her complaint attributed, not certified as an audited account.

Five hundred cash is offered for a dish whose ingredients she estimates at twenty or thirty cash. The surplus becomes a deliberate allowance for incidental kitchen demands; it is not the market price of the dish.

True rose-essence chain: Bao-yu authorizes Aroma to give the remaining bottle to Parfumée, who gives it to Wu-er. Mrs Liu pours some for her nephew. Lady Wang's missing essence is a separate gift theft by Cai-yun. True frost chain: official's gate gift, Wu-er's uncle's share, his wife, Mrs Liu, Wu-er, half the frost, wrapped separately in paper and passed via Swallow to Parfumée. The remaining kitchen packet is seized. Patience's later Bao-yu origin story is a cover.

Forty blows for mother and daughter, disposal of Wu-er, and later kneeling on shards in the sun without food are ordered or proposed but not carried out. Detention lasts one night. Do not turn the threatened acts into completed punishment.

Patience explicitly says the pregnancy ended at six or seven months. Chapter 55 says miscarriage without naming the gestational month. Preserve both texts; do not supply a modern diagnosis or change the number.

Qin Xian's wife reports two shi of rice missing, an extra month's ordinary rice issued and a charcoal shortfall. Her gifts are separately one basket of charcoal, five hundred catties of firewood and one load of polished rice. Do not sum shortages and bribes or turn a load into a verified exact weight.

Wang Zi-teng sends a set of clothes, shoes and stockings, one hundred birthday peaches and one hundred bundles of fine noodles. Xi-feng's purse holds a gold longevity figure and a Persian toy. These are not automatically the mechanical boat later mentioned. Zhang's gifts of four kinds and Xue Ke's four kinds are separate lists; neither expression alone fixes the total number of individual objects.

The four joint celebrants are Bao-yu, Bao-qin, Xiu-yan and Patience. No month or day of this shared birthday is supplied. Yuan-chun and the ancestral elder share New Year's Day; Lady Wang is third-month first day and Jia Lian ninth day; Dai-yu and Aroma second-month twelfth day. Do not infer a shared precise date for Grandmother Jia and Bao-chai from the Lantern Festival comment.

Two extra tables are ordered for Patience, while four tables finally seat the whole party. Preserve the seating: the four celebrants with Tan-chun and Faithful; Bao-chai, Dai-yu, Xiang-yun, Ying-chun, Xi-chun, Caltrop and Silver; You-shi, Li Wan, Aroma and Cai-yun; Nightingale, Oriole, Skybright, Xiao-luo, Chess and others. Aunt Xue is separately in the council hall.

Three failed guesses cost one cup. Bao-qin and Caltrop both throw three; other matching dice totals are not always given. Bao-yu drinks an extra cup for Dai-yu to compose his answer. Do not invent the number or faces of dice.

The fallen fan is on the ground, petals cover her clothes and a scarf of petals forms the pillow. Xiang-yun takes two cups of strong tea, holds a sobering stone in her mouth and drinks some sour soup. Preserve sequence without promising efficacy.
Aroma brings exactly two fresh cups. Bao-yu takes one; Bao-chai drinks a mouthful from the other, leaving half a cup for Dai-yu, who finishes it. Another cup is offered but not actually brought.

Parfumée requests one bowl of soup and half a bowl of rice. The delivery includes four pastries. Parfumée eats one bowl of soup-soaked rice and two pieces of goose; Bao-yu takes one pastry and half a bowl of rice; Swallow eats leftovers and keeps two pastries for her mother. The fourth pastry's exact fate is unstated. Bao-yu later eats another half-bowl with tea.
Parfumée says she formerly drank two or three catties of Huiquan wine. This is a boast about past capacity, not a present measured intake or a conversion to litres.

Bao-qin supplies the material from which Bao-chai and Caltrop each have a skirt. Aroma's matching skirt was made last month but unworn during mourning. Aroma brings it herself and takes the dirty skirt away. The buried things are the paired orchid and caltrop flowers.

Four senior maids contribute five qian of silver each, totalling two taels. Four junior maids contribute three qian each, adding one tael two qian. Total three taels two qian; eight contributors; forty dishes; one jar of Shaoxing wine from Patience. The leave or absence parenthesis does not subtract one of the eight or introduce counterfeit money.

Lot sequence and dice totals: Bao-chai 5, Tan-chun 16, Li Wan 19, Xiang-yun 18 thrown by Dai-yu, Musk 9, Caltrop 19, Dai-yu 6, Aroma 20. No lot is drawn for Bao-yu. Flower rules are separately recorded; under Musk's lot, everyone takes three mouthfuls in place of three cups.

After the second watch, eleven clock strokes and 子初初刻十分 are given together. Preserve the period wording; do not assert an exact modern 23:10 conversion. Continued drinking reaches the fourth watch. Aroma sleeps on the opposite couch after moving Parfumée.

Xiu-yan and Adamantina were neighbours for ten years. The card is delivered by an older woman, held by Si-er and forgotten until next morning. Bao-yu writes a reply and puts it through the gate; no meeting takes place.

You-shi estimates at least half a month before Jia Zhen can arrive, but he later rides back at speed with no precise elapsed day count. Mourning opens three days later. The coffin enters the city on the fourth day of an unspecified lunar month, departing at mao and arriving between wei and shen. Its subsequent return to the temple and removal to the family's native place after the hundred days are separate stages. Do not calculate an unstated calendar from these markers.

Funeral expenses: 1,110 taels total, 500 already paid, 610 outstanding. The Zhen gift is a separate 500, of which 200 is spent and 300 sent home. The implied further shortfall is 310, but that derived figure must not replace the actual dialogue's figures. Jia Lian later makes up the money.

The earlier betrothal was arranged before birth; contact has lapsed for more than ten years. Jia Rong first estimates a payoff of ten-odd taels; the actual coerced cancellation costs twenty. The proposed two servant households become one named couple in the actual setup. The house has over twenty rooms, roughly two li behind Ning-Rong Street, with two newly bought maids.

The wedding is fixed for the third day of an unspecified lunar month. The mother and younger sister move in on its second day; You Er-jie arrives before dawn the following day. Five taels per month supports the new household; Jia Lian transfers his private savings. There are ten or so residents. About two months pass before Jia Zhen visits. No exact month is supplied.

Two horses must be tethered separately. Three pages share the kang. The second-gate rota has two groups of four, eight men. Joker says Patience was one of four dowry maids, now the only one left; two prior chambermaids were expelled within six months. His once-in-one-or-two-years estimate remains hearsay.
Two kinds of needlework gifts are named at 57.36; the total number of pieces is unstated. Preserve the distinction between kinds and individual objects.

literary.guidance: Keep each parallel pair and the source's tonal contrasts. At 61, 瞒赃 concerns concealment of the theft affair, not dirt or stolen money alone. At 62, peony bedding and the red skirt are image anchors. At 63, private celebration turns suddenly to death. At 64, poems and jade courtship balance. At 65, the title's Liu reference must not be expanded into an explanation inside the still-uninformed dialogue.

Retain the granary rat and crow borrowing grain; the rat and precious vessel image; the charcoal basket flatterer's metaphor; the fly and cracked egg; and knowing when to let go. Translate their usable force in natural English while keeping distinctive concrete images. Do not silently replace difficult Chinese with another idiom.

The concealed-word game uses a shared unspoken bridge. 老 and 药 meet through 圃; 人 and 窗 point to 鸡, answered through 埘; 瓢 and 绿 are merely said to be understood, so no invented poem is put in a character's mouth; 宝 and 钗 meet through 玉. Preserve the quoted evidence and name play. A short explanatory note may clarify the rules, not replace the scene.

Dai-yu answers for Bao-yu with five parts: classical prose, old poetry, domino name, tune title and almanac phrase. Preserve all five in order and the two-line hazelnut versus fulling-block pun. Do not treat the composite as one quotation by one ancient author.

Xiang-yun's five-part answer follows the same rule with waves, chains, boat, wind and a no-travel almanac warning. Her duck-head and maid pun turns on sound; keep the girls' objection and osmanthus hair oil. A minimal note is preferable to replacing the duck with an English pun object.
The sleepy five-part answer keeps 泉香而酒冽, 玉盏盛来琥珀光, 梅梢月上, 醉扶归 and 宜会亲友 as successive sources. Preserve 玉盏, the current source's cup, instead of silently restoring the better-known 玉碗 variant.

Keep the paired plant names and order: Guanyin willow and arhat pine; gentleman's bamboo and beauty's canna; starry green and monthly red; peony from The Peony Pavilion and loquat from The Lute; sisters' flowers and married-couple orchids. Explain the pipa sound echo only if needed; never substitute invented Western plants.

Bao-chai's peony lot has its image, four-character heading, one verse line and communal toast. Keep the interrupted birthday-song opening as only one line, then the complete quoted 赏花时 and continuation. The public Handan play identifies He Xian-gu addressing Lü Dong-bin but does not authorize importing different Chinese readings or supplying omitted dialogue.

All eight lots retain image, title, poem, rule, drinkers and reaction. Translate the repeated peony line identically when Bao-yu repeats it. Li Wan passes the dice to the next player. Xiang-yun is exempt while neighbours drink; Bao-yu passes half to Parfumée and Dai-yu tips hers out. Under Musk's lot, everyone takes three mouthfuls in place of three cups.

Do not turn Tan-chun's noble-husband lot into a narrator-certified future marriage. Its joke about a princess is what the party says now. Caltrop's paired blossom has no stated botanical species. Hibiscus remains a working, not uniquely demonstrated, identification of Dai-yu's 芙蓉. Preserve the flower images and Aroma's peach without attaching later plot outcomes.

Both private cards must be complete, including self-designations and humble courtesies. The threshold couplet's iron threshold and earth mound or earthen bun must support the 槛外/槛内 contrast and echo Temple of the Iron Threshold. Keep 畸人/世人 as a second contrast, based on Xiu-yan's account rather than a newly composed philosophical essay.

Preserve 雄奴/匈奴, 耶律/野驴, 韦大英/惟大英雄 and 荳童/琴童 sound and semantic play with brief in-prose support or conditional notes. Bao-yu's historical and ethnic claims are not corrected into a modern history lesson and are not endorsed by the translation.

The Board of Rites memorial and imperial edict are nested quoted documents. The edict runs through 钦此 in 63.55. Preserve degree, inherited office, official leave, fifth-rank posthumous grant, city entry, return home, Court of Imperial Entertainments offering and permission for mourning visits. Do not invent a complete original document beyond the supplied text.

Five headings and twenty seven-character lines are required. Xi Shi contrasts the vanished beauty with the old woman still washing silk; Lady Yu contrasts the sword with later humiliation; Ming-fei questions the emperor's delegated power; Green Pearl questions her patron's valuation; Red Whisk recognises the obscure hero and escapes the moribund patron. Let those arguments govern the verse, not generic tragic-beauty sentiment.

重瞳 and 乌骓 evoke Xiang Yu; 黥彭 are Qing Bu or Ying Bu and Peng Yue; 石尉 is Shi Chong; 杨公 is Yang Su; Red Whisk's chosen poor man is Li Jing. These identify allusions, not prove every legendary event. Preserve the poems' own rhetoric about execution and affection rather than treating it as documentary history.

Bao-chai quotes two lines by Wang An-shi and two by Ouyang Xiu; all four remain complete and attributed at the level the source supplies. The closing couplet keeps the related branches, joined marriage branches and weapons metaphor. Prose layout does not permit dropping quoted lines.

Keep the baked-cakes bed-sharing obscenity, noodle-water and shadow-puppet metaphors, stolen gong, ox bezoar and dog treasure, fire-and-knife opposition, vinegar vessels, rose thorns, sickly Xi Shi and snow-heap beauty. Render insults at their actual intensity. Do not replace uncertainty with a choreographed sexual event or modern psychological diagnosis.

materials.subject: Eggs, tofu and kitchen dishes
materials.guidance: Keep eggs for steaming separate from the reserve for garnishes. Preserve rancid tofu as Lotus's allegation; mugwort shoots, wheat gluten, pickled radish and wolfberry shoots are not interchangeable vegetables. The water-board is a reusable written menu board, not a water supply.

materials.subject: Rose essence and fuling frost
materials.guidance: Reuse the established roots rose essence and fuling frost. They are different gifts with different transfer chains and should not become generic medicine or perfume. Medical benefits are claimed by characters, not endorsed.

materials.subject: Birthday objects
materials.guidance: Keep the ritual name-token, paper longevity figure, prayers, annual lock and life-star references without turning them into Christian baptism or an ordinary padlock. The palace-made purse, gold longevity figure and Persian toy are distinct objects.

materials.subject: Seat, scarf and tea tray
materials.guidance: The peony flowers cushion a stone seat figuratively; the scarf actually encloses petals as a pillow. The fan falls to the ground. The little fitted Western-lacquer tea tray holds two cups; do not add silverwork or extra vessels.

materials.subject: The delivered meal
materials.guidance: Retain shrimp-ball and chicken-skin soup, duck steamed with fermented rice, cured rouge-coloured goose breast, four cream-and-pine-kernel flaky rolls and fragrant green-grained rice. Do not substitute modern dishes or infer that every adjective names a certified cultivar.

materials.subject: Pomegranate-red silk damask
materials.guidance: 绫 is silk damask or figured silk in the established material family. Keep pomegranate red as colour, not a fruit pattern. Distinguish skirt, underclothes, knee trousers and shoe uppers threatened by the mud. No amount of fabric is stated.

materials.subject: Tables, textiles and jewellery
materials.guidance: The round huali kang table is moved onto the kang; do not call every huali wood rosewood of a precise species. The blue-green lined gauze pillow is filled with peony petals. Bao-yu's red cotton-gauze jacket and ink-spattered green damask trousers differ from Parfumée's patchwork satin jacket, green sash and floral pink trousers.

materials.subject: The patchwork jacket
materials.guidance: 水田 describes joined patches resembling paddy fields. The compressed wording 玉色红青酡绒三色缎子 does not securely settle the segmentation of every colour and material term. Preserve the little lined patchwork jacket and its three-colour satin construction. Keep the complete Chinese compound in the working note; do not assert that 酡绒 is a separate fabric or finish, substitute 驼绒, or invent a precise textile specification.

materials.subject: Dishes and lots
materials.guidance: Forty small pale-white Ding-ware dishes are saucer-sized. The carved bamboo cylinder holds ivory flower lots. Each lot has a flower image, title, quoted verse and instruction; these are not ordinary playing cards.

materials.subject: Costume and glass
materials.guidance: The shaved sides, central hair arrangement, fur headband, small military boots and thick-soled shoes are costume details. Bao-yu's claim about gold-flecked glass and Wen-du-li-na is reported foreign lore. Do not identify an exact modern country or laboratory mineral; keep material glass separate from Parfumée's nickname.

materials.subject: Elixirs and funerary objects
materials.guidance: Keep breathing practice, stellar observances, gengshen vigil and cinnabar or gold ingestion in historical discourse. The physicians and Daoists disagree in register and explanation; do not add a modern toxicological diagnosis. Litter, prepared coffin, mourning clothes and ceremonial rank remain distinct.

materials.subject: Mourning fan-case, cooled tea and ritual vessel
materials.guidance: Aroma makes a grey cord for a replacement fan-case, not a fan itself. A teapot is cooled in repeatedly changed well-water, never ice. 龙文鼒 is a small tripod vessel with a dragon design; its placement supports ritual preparation without naming the offering's recipient.

materials.subject: Betel purse and nine-dragon pendant
materials.guidance: The betel purse is tied to a silk handkerchief; Jia Lian takes half-chewed betel, keeps the rest and ties his Han jade nine-dragon pendant onto the cloth before returning it. Treat Han as the source's antique attribution, not a modern authenticated provenance. The funeral silver is a separate transaction.

materials.subject: Plain wedding clothes and later adornment
materials.guidance: Plain chairs and dress coexist with prepared wedding articles and illicit mourning-time marriage. Preserve the younger sister's partly open jacket, green breast-cover, red shoes, earrings and tiny bound feet without adding bodily detail. Her destruction of clothes and demand for costly jewellery are narrated acts, not a price list.

relationships.guidance: The gate boy uses aunt and sister as familiar servant addresses. Neither the taunt about another uncle nor his sister address for Wu-er establishes a literal new relationship.
Xiao-chan is the same Chan-jie known through Mamma Xia; Lotus is Chess's subordinate messenger, not Chan-jie. Swallow and Xiao-yan are the same person.
Qin Xian's wife is Chess's paternal uncle's wife. Chess's parents belong to Jia She's branch; her uncle serves the other branch. Do not assign the whole family to one establishment.
Aunt Zhao is Tan-chun's mother and Jia Huan's mother. The protective reference to the third girl means Tan-chun, not a third unnamed thief.
Four people share this birthday: Bao-yu, Bao-qin, Xiu-yan and Patience. Xiang-yun identifies them but is not a fifth birthday celebrant. Bao-qin and Xue Ke remain siblings, not spouses.
老太太和宝姐姐他们娘儿两个 uses an affectionate senior-and-junior pairing. Bao-chai is not Grandmother Jia's daughter, and this line does not establish an exact shared birth date for them.
Cai-er, Xi-chun's little maid, is not Cai-yun. The accused woman is Cai-er's mother.
Zhen-er serves Caltrop; Zhuan-er serves Xiu-yan. The Second Miss whom Zhen-er mentions is not securely named by this sentence; preserve the title.

Caltrop, Skybright and Bao-chai are said to be Aroma's age; Dai-yu shares Aroma's birthday; Parfumée says she too has the surname Hua. Keep these distinct grounds for drinking rather than making everyone born the same day.
Parfumée belongs to Bao-yu, Kui-guan to Xiang-yun and Dou-guan to Bao-qin. Renaming does not create new male servants. The Glass alias is Parfumée alone here, not the actual Glass of author 83.10.
Pei-feng and Xie-yuan are Jia Zhen's two concubines, brought by You-shi. They are not You-shi's step-sisters.

You-shi's stepmother brought You Er-jie and You San-jie from her earlier marriage. They are You-shi's step-sisters, not daughters of the same mother or necessarily of her father. Jia Rong uses maternal-grandmother and maternal-aunt kin terms through You-shi's position as Jia Zhen's wife.

The source states earlier sexual impropriety and gives further implications. Preserve the facts and source judgments at their actual places; do not turn every inference into a documented sexual act or adopt another edition's contrary backstory.

Bao Er is the established servant. His earlier wife died in chapter 44; the current wife is not thereby the dead woman. This source does not narrate her acquisition or a second wedding here. Do not import the public composite passage.

尤氏姐妹 at 64.43 means You Er-jie and You San-jie, not You-shi, who remains at the temple. 尤氏母女 at 65.5 means the mother and younger daughter, before You Er-jie joins them. 尤氏 at 65.31 means You Er-jie. 尤氏姊妹 at 65.36 means You Er-jie and You San-jie. You-shi is absent from all four scenes.
Long-er serves Jia Lian; Xi-er and Shou-er accompany Jia Zhen. This Xi-er is a male page, not the female Xi-er seen with Oriole in chapter 35.

Joker reports the family relationships and servant arrangements with limited access. His estimate about Patience's intimacy and his generalizations about all family members are attributed claims, not a new omniscient family register.

Keep the approximate two months and the seventh-month speculation separate. selectedReaderNotes.text: The song is from Tang Xian-zu’s The Handan Dream, where the immortal He Xian-gu addresses Lü Dong-bin.

selectedReaderNotes.subject: The last flower of spring
selectedReaderNotes.text: Tumi is a climbing, rose-like flower that blooms late in spring.

selectedReaderNotes.subject: Names behind the five poems
selectedReaderNotes.text: The double-pupilled lord is Xiang Yu; Qing Bu is Ying Bu. Commandant Shi is Shi Chong, Green Pearl’s patron. Lord Yang is Yang Su, whom Red Whisk leaves for Li Jing. The poems freely recast received stories.

anchor.text: ‘Each found a view of his own, unlike anyone else’s. Cousin Lin’s five poems today may also be said to have fresh conceptions and to open up new ground.’

readerNotePolicy: Use only these three selected texts, immediately after the complete specified segments. Selection does not assert that the notes or chapters have been installed. Do not add a recipient for Dai-yu's private offering, future flower-lot outcomes, an absent remarriage story or duplicated explanations.

interpretiveLimits.guidance: Colloquial images, name jokes and folk physiology are contextual expressions. The plums-and-sweat complaint is not objective physiology; some sound and lexical play cannot be carried over completely.

Standard endgame move, leave or absence, secure patchwork-and-satin details and hibiscus are bounded readings. Do not invent a board position, absent maid, Latin species or certain interpretation of the compressed textile compound.
The coarse bodily rendering innards is broad and loses a specific egg or child resonance. No pregnancy or actual injury is established.

The morning offering, palace remembrance and Er-jie as the person sitting are defensible contextual readings, not uniquely proved parses. The seating interpretation has moderate confidence; contrary commentary remains possible.
Dai-yu makes a private offering. Its recipient is unknown; neither the narration nor a note may settle it.
Preserve the locally supplied counts and unreported entrances without inventing a harmonized sequence.
Retain the source's omission of Bao Er's remarriage account, give the glue-and-lacquer idiom natural English, and keep the black-hen proverb and anxious denial as bounded contextual renderings.

Accusations, self-serving excuses and Joker's household portrait remain attributed speech with partial knowledge. Lady Xing is the mother-in-law in Joker's reported complaint at 65.28; naming her does not certify the complaint.

continuityPolicy: Use the project's own earlier chapters and chapters 81–85 for verified identities, diction and explicit recollections. Do not import later events or knowledge. Joker at 65.25–39 is the same role-and-relationship identity as the project's own 84.39; this is not a generic replacement of Xing.
preservationPolicy: Every earlier term and voice object, earlier batch and the existing standard is preserved. This supplement applies only in its stated scenes and senses.
reviewPolicy: At each five-chapter checkpoint, read all bilingual units and then the continuous English. After narrow changes, read complete affected units and necessary contexts. Coverage and hashes do not replace semantic or literary judgment.
